oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: log-alert.rule.high-latency triggered 42 times in last 5m for service=ingest (priority=P1) - paging oncall
oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-20260315-4219 - paging Maya R (primary)
Maya R: on it, joining console now. Any customer pages?
Ethan C: seeing spikes on ingest-write errors too, correlating with latency, looks like a flood of 502s from a downstream cache cluster
Lina S: +1, dashboards show versioned deploy 2026.03.10 rolled on a subset of hosts 5m before spike
Maya R: okay starting live mitigation. First step: mute high-volume non-customer errors for 10m to stop pager noise while we triage
Maya R: quick note — will adjust log alert filter to exclude known benign stacktrace from heartbeat-checker (temp)
Jon V: please paste the exact query change you plan so we can review
Maya R: going to apply this replacement in the log query:
Maya R: ```
# original filter
service:ingest AND status:502 | count by host
# temp change to reduce noise
service:ingest AND status:502 AND NOT message =~ /heartbeat-checker|health-ping/ | count by host
```
Ethan C: good call, heartbeat noise was 60% of triggered events in the last 5m
SRE-Triage-Bot: @Maya R created task TKT-4283 "Investigate 502 flood and patch downstream cache" assigned to Ethan C, due 2026-03-17
Maya R: applied filter and temporarily disabled escalation in the alert policy (10m window). watching metrics
Lina S: dashboards look quieter already, pages stopped. latency still elevated but now we have fewer false positives to focus on root cause
Maya R: live mitigation note: added regex exclude for heartbeat in alert rule and lowered sensitivity on anomaly detector for ingest by +20% threshold to avoid immediate re-pages
Ethan C: digging into cache cluster — seeing connection churn to backend DB during the same timeframe. I'm spinning up a focused query:
Ethan C: ```
index=ingest logs | where host in (cache-*) and timestamp > now()-15m | stats count by error_code, backend_host
```
Jon V: can we route traffic away from affected cache nodes as a precaution?
Lina S: yes, I can trigger a rolling drain for cache nodes cache-12 and cache-13 if we confirm they're the culprits
Maya R: go for it Lina, coordinate with Ethan on the list to drain
Lina S: draining cache-12 now. cache-12 -> draining :spinner:
Ethan C: confirmed cache-12 had elevated connection reset counts to db-3; draining reduced resets by ~70%
Maya R: good. I'll extend the temporary alert suppression for another 30m while we stabilize and create a post-incident alert tuning PR for a permanent rule update
Maya R: follow-up actions (quick):
- reopen alert rule for edit with suggested query changes
- add regex signature to exclude heartbeat-checker permanently if safe
- create dashboard panels for connection-reset rates per cache node
- run canary rollout for downstream cache patch
Jon V: please capture the exact Datadog/LogQL rule text in the PR and include a before/after false-positive rate measured from the last 24h
Maya R: will do. I'll also attach sample logs that matched the heartbeat signature so reviewers can validate
SRE-Triage-Bot: Note: On-call Handoff scheduled to Ethan C at 11:00 UTC.
Maya R: handing off context to Ethan — I'm going to sleep; everything stable for now but please escalate if pages resume
Ethan C: taking over. I've filed TKT-4284 for long-term alert refinement and TKT-4285 for postmortem write-up.
Lina S: I'll follow up with a dashboard PR and include a quick runbook entry on how to mute these alerts safely during noisy incidents
Jon V: thumbs up. Also, can we add an automated signature detection for this heartbeat noise so it never re-triggers large-scale paging?
Maya R: yes that's the plan in TKT-4284 — we will add a regex signature and a unit test against a golden log set before merging
Ethan C: last note — customers impacted: 3 small SaaS tenants experienced delayed writes ~2-5m window. CS notified via status page update at 10:42 UTC.
Maya R: thanks team — will drop a short incident summary in #incidents later.
oncall-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident INC-20260315-4219 status: Mitigated - follow-ups created
